summary.intent: Perform a security review of the feat/store-ipns-crypto-data-in-db branch (IPNS signature/pubkey storage), implement all high and medium fixes, and merge via PR.
summary.outcome: All HIGH and MEDIUM findings were fixed and pushed to PR #448. A follow-up CJS/ESM compatibility breakage in CI was resolved by bundling ESM-only libp2p dependencies into the @cipherbox/crypto CJS output via tsup noExternal config.

repo: The IPNS service (apps/web and sdk-core) is a thin client-side wrapper: heavy crypto lives in @cipherbox/crypto, record marshaling in sdk-core, and the API only relays pre-signed bytes to the DHT.
IPNS names are cryptographically derived from the Ed25519 public key via deriveIpnsName() — the server never has access to private keys (zero-knowledge model).
@cipherbox/crypto's CJS build was externalizing @libp2p/crypto which is ESM-only, causing ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED in the NestJS (CommonJS) API.
The tsup config for @cipherbox/crypto required noExternal: ['@libp2p/crypto', '@libp2p/crypto/keys'] to inline bundle these ESM-only deps into the CJS output.
The web app had a divergent base64 encoding pattern (spread operator) that had already been fixed in sdk-core but not in apps/web.

code.finding: resolveIpnsRecord verified Ed25519 signature validity but never verified that the returned pubKey corresponded to the requested ipnsName — allowing a compromised server to substitute its own keypair and pass verification.
Used spread operator (String.fromCharCode(...new Uint8Array())) for base64 encoding which causes call-stack overflow on large IPNS records; sdk-core already used a for-loop instead.
publish() did not derive or send publicKey to the API, meaning server-side binding validation and client-side resolve signature verification were dead code for web-published records.
Server stored publicKey but never validated that it matches the IPNS name (derived deterministically from the key). Added server-side binding check as defense-in-depth.
MaxLength(100) on publicKey field was inconsistent — a raw 32-byte Ed25519 key encodes to exactly 44 base64 chars; updated to MaxLength(64) to reject malformed oversized inputs.
noExternal config was missing for @libp2p/crypto and @libp2p/crypto/keys — these ESM-only packages must be bundled into the CJS output to work in NestJS (CommonJS) consumers.

workflow: The security review command spawns parallel sub-agents: one for vulnerability discovery, then one per finding for false-positive filtering — confidence < 8 findings are dropped.
CI failures from ESM/CJS incompatibility are best fixed at the package build level (tsup noExternal) rather than using dynamic import() at call sites.
Running `node -e "require('./dist/index.cjs').deriveIpnsName"` is a quick sanity check that CJS bundling worked before pushing.

friction: CI caught a runtime ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED error that local builds did not surface — @libp2p/crypto is ESM-only but NestJS consumes CJS, and tsup was externalizing it.
User rejected the dynamic import() workaround, requiring a proper tsup bundling fix instead.
The session was interrupted mid-edit (dynamic import attempt was typed but never committed before the user redirected).
Context window pressure: the full diff was 109.6KB and had to be read from a persisted output file rather than inline.
open_items: Finding #4 (signature verification downgrade — server can omit signature fields causing signatureVerified: false, and callers don't gate on this boolean) was explicitly deferred as a design decision.
Finding #5 (inconsistent key zeroization across crypto functions) was deferred as a convention/debt issue rather than an acute vulnerability.
The @cipherbox/crypto tsup noExternal change bundles libp2p into the CJS output — the bundle size impact should be assessed if CJS consumers are size-sensitive.
Consider adding a CI step that verifies CJS require() of the crypto package works, to catch future ESM-only transitive dependency additions early.
